claim: Citadelle de Namur is open daily 10am-6pm from 1 April to 27 September 2026 (closed 20 May, 3-5 July, 21 September); the 3-attraction Citadel Pass (underground galleries OR Middle Ages tour + tourist train + Terra Nova visitor centre) costs €22 adult / €20 child, and the 4-attraction pass €36/€32.
quote: From 1 April to 27 September: Open Monday to Sunday from 10am to 6pm. Closed on 20 May, 3, 4 and 5 July and 21 September. Citadel Pass (3 visits) €22 / €20. Citadel Pass (4 visits) €36 / €32.

claim: Parking at the Citadelle de Namur Esplanade is free and unlimited except during events, but Route Merveilleuse between Terra Nova and the Esplanade is closed for works until end of March 2026.
quote: Parking at the Esplanade is free and available permanently except during certain events ... Route Merveilleuse is inaccessible between Terra Nova and the Esplanade until the end of March 2026.

claim: The Terra Nova Visitor Centre, housed in the former 1820-1825 Dutch barracks on the Citadelle de Namur site, presents 2000 years of Namur and European military history via a floating wall of screens, a plan-relief scale model and audio guides in six languages, and is accessible to people with reduced mobility.
quote: In the old Terra Nova barracks, visitors walk along a floating wall of screens and images that narrate the story of life in Namur from the dawn of time to the present day ... 2000 years of European urban and military history ... Audio guides are available in French, Dutch, English, German, Spanish and Chinese.

claim: Citadelle de Dinant is open daily 10am-6pm April-September and 10am-4:30pm October-March; standard ticket including HistoPad augmented-reality guide is €15 adult / €13 child (4-12), with a 3-in-1 package adding a 45-minute Meuse cruise at €25 adult / €20 child; recommended self-guided visit is ~1h30.
quote: April to September: Daily 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM. October to March: Daily 10:00 AM – 4:30 PM. Standard Visit (includes HistoPad): Adult €15.00, Child (ages 4-12) €13.00. 3-in-1 Package (Citadel + HistoPad + 45-minute cruise): €25.00/adult, €20.00/child. Around 1 hour 30 minutes.

claim: Two free car/coach parking areas, EV charging points and a bike rack are available at the top of the Citadelle de Dinant, but the cable car is closed for major renovation, so visitors arrive by car at the summit or climb the 408-step staircase from the town centre.
quote: Two complimentary parking areas for cars and coaches. Bike rack at the top of the site. Electric vehicle charging points available ... A historic 408-step staircase connects Dinant town centre directly to the fortress.

claim: Château de Vêves at Celles (Houyet) is open Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays 10am-5pm from 30 March to 1 November 2026, daily during Flemish Easter holidays (6-19 April), daily 6 July-23 August, and daily during All Saints holidays 19 October-1 November; last admission 4:30pm.
quote: From 30 March to 01 November 2026 The Castle is open on Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays from 10:00 am to 5:00 pm ... From 6 July to 23 August 2026 The Castle is open every day (Monday to Sunday) from 10:00 to 17:00 ... The Castle closes at 5:00 pm (last admission at 4:30 pm).

claim: Château de Vêves admission is €9.50 adult, €8.50 senior/student/teacher, €6.50 child (under 4 free); group rate (20+) €8 adult / €6 child; optional treasure hunt +€2.75, and children are dressed as knights and princesses free of charge during the visit.
quote: Adults: €9.50 - Seniors (60+), students, teachers: €8.50 - Children: €6.50 - Children under 4: Free. Treasure hunt option: +€2.75 per person. All children are dressed free as knights and princesses during their visit.

claim: Château de Freÿr near Hastière is open Thursday-Sunday and public holidays 11am-5pm from 4 April to 15 November 2026, with extended Tuesday-Sunday opening 1 July-31 August; admission €12 adult, €10 senior/student/adolescent, free for children under 12 with adult; on-site parking for cars, coaches and bikes; last entry 45 minutes before closing.
quote: April 4 – November 15: Thursday–Sunday & public holidays, 11:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. July 1 – August 31: Tuesday–Sunday & public holidays, 11:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m. Adult €12, Senior/Adolescent/Student €10, Children (up to 12 years, with adult) Free. Parking for coach buses, cars, bikes.

claim: Freÿr is a 16th-17th century Renaissance château on the Meuse facing the Freÿr cliffs whose 30,000 m² French-style gardens hold 9 ponds, 33 orange trees still in their 18th-century crates, hornbeam labyrinth hedges and a Moretti-decorated pavilion — classed as Wallonia's protected heritage.
quote: Freÿr is a Renaissance castle ... The French-style gardens feature flowerbeds and arbours, ponds, fountains and orange trees set against the impressive backdrop of the Meuse and its cliffs. The gardens comprise 30,000 m² of hedges, 9 ponds, 33 orange trees and a pavilion decorated by the Moretti brothers.

claim: Château de Lavaux-Sainte-Anne (near Rochefort, ~40km from Profondeville so just outside the 30km radius) opens Wed-Sun 10am-6pm (daily in school holidays), last entry 4:45pm; €9.50 adult / €8.50 senior-student / €6 child (3-12, costume included); free on-site parking; 1-3h visit covering 32 furnished rooms across three museums (Lords of Lavaux, rural Famenne, nature/hunting) plus French gardens and a wetland reserve.
quote: Opens Wednesday-Sunday, 10 am–6 pm year-round (last entry 4:45 pm) ... Adult: €9.50, Senior (65+)/Student: €8.50, Child (3–12): €6 (includes costume rental). Free parking available on-site. Between 1 and 3 hours. 32 furnished and decorated rooms across three museums.

claim: Château de Spontin in Yvoir (in the Bocq valley ~12km east of Profondeville) opens Tue-Sun 10am-5pm in July-August, Wed/Sat/Sun 2pm-5pm in September-October, and daily 2pm-5pm (except Mon) from 28 April during spring break; €8 adult, €5 child under 12, guided group €7pp — but private events may close it unexpectedly so call ahead.
quote: July & August: Tuesday-Sunday, 10am-5pm. September & October: Wednesday, Saturday, Sunday, 2pm-5pm. Spring break (from April 28): Daily 2pm-5pm except Mondays. Adults: €8, Children (under 12): €5. Certain weekends or opening days may be exceptionally closed to the public.

claim: The 13th-century feudal Château de Spontin is one of the rare castles in Belgium to preserve a still-functioning authentic drawbridge, was reopened to visitors after years of closure following its purchase by a private owner, and sits beside the scenic Bocq tourist railway in the valley.
quote: Le château féodal de Spontin ... est l'un des rares châteaux de Belgique à avoir conservé un authentique pont-levis en état de fonctionnement.

claim: Château de Lavaux-Sainte-Anne is about 29 km by road from Dinant (which itself is 15 km from Profondeville), making the total drive from Arbre/Profondeville roughly 40-45 km — just outside the strict 30 km radius but still a feasible day-trip add-on.
quote: The distance between Dinant and Château de Lavaux-Sainte-Anne is 13 miles (approximately 21 kilometers), with a road distance of 17.8 miles (approximately 29 kilometers). It takes approximately 21 minutes to drive.

claim: Profondeville sits ~12-15 km south of Namur and ~15 km north of Dinant on the N92 along the Meuse, placing Citadelle de Namur, Citadelle de Dinant, Château de Freÿr (~22 km), Château de Spontin (~12 km), Château de Vêves at Celles (~20-25 km) all within the 30 km radius; Bouillon at ~66-88 km is well outside.
quote: Profondeville et Namur ... 12.5 km ... 17 minutes ... La distance en ligne droite entre Bouillon et Profondeville est 65.10 km, mais la distance à parcourir en voiture est de 88 km.

claim: Maredsous Abbey's Saint-Joseph reception centre is open every day of the year except 1 January, weekdays 11:00-18:00 and weekends/public holidays 10:00-19:00.
quote: OPEN EACH DAY OF THE YEAR EXCEPT ON JANUARY THE 1ST ... Opened from 11 o'clock until 18 o'clock ... Opened from 10 o'clock until 19 o'clock

claim: The Saint-Joseph reception offers a 1h30 guided tasting visit of the micro-brewery and hop field with special on-site-only beers, plus a cafeteria serving Maredsous beer, cheese and bread.
quote: a tasting visit (1h30) offers a guided discovery of the micro-brewery and hop field, with special beers available for tasting only on site

claim: Jardins d'Annevoie open April-October daily 09:30-17:30; adult admission €9.50, children €5.50; group rate €11 adults.
quote: From April to October: open daily from 9:30 AM to 5:30 PM ... adult admission is €9.50 and children are €5.50

claim: Annevoie's gardens were begun around 1758 by Charles-Alexis de Montpellier and blend French formality, Italian water-as-soul layout and English Romantic naturalism — designated Major Walloon Heritage between 1992-2009.
quote: French approach: Formal perspectives without curves ... Italian approach: Natural variety integrated into the landscape, with water as 'the soul of the gardens' ... English approach: Artificially created natural effects

claim: Annevoie's 50 water features have run continuously since 1758 without pumps, using only gravity — engineering reputed superior to Versailles, and the only historical water gardens in Belgium.
quote: The 50 water features in this garden all work without any pumps and machinery and rely on the laws of gravity

claim: Floreffe Abbey's Moulin-Brasserie is open year-round daily 11:00-18:00 (weekends until 20:00); abbey-church guided tours run 1 April-30 September at 13:30, 14:30, 16:00 and 17:00 (€8 including guide), and a self-guided exterior booklet costs €5.
quote: Le moulin-brasserie est ouvert tous les jours de 11h à 18h ... Les visites de l'abbatiale se font à 13h30, 14h30, 16h et 17h ... Le prix de la visite, guidage inclus, est 8,00 €

claim: TreM.a (Musée des Arts anciens du Namurois, rue de Fer 24 in central Namur) opens Tuesday-Sunday 10:00-13:00 and 13:30-18:00; €5 adult permanent (€8 with temporary exhibition), free the first Sunday of each month.
quote: Du mardi au dimanche 10h00 – 13h00 / 13h30 – 18h00 ... Adults: €5 (permanent collections only) or €8 (with temporary exhibitions) ... First Sunday of each month: Free for all

claim: TreM.a houses the Trésor d'Oignies — gold-and-silver liturgical work by Hugo d'Oignies and his workshop (c. 1225-1250) — alongside sculptures by the Master of Waha and paintings by Henri Bles.
quote: medieval treasures of the priory of Saint-Nicolas d'Oignies ... created by the goldsmith Hugo d'Oignies or his workshop between approximately 1225-1250

claim: Musée Félicien Rops in Namur opens Tuesday-Sunday 10:00-18:00 (daily in July-August); combined ticket €5 (€2.50 reduced); closed 24-25 Dec, 31 Dec, 1 Jan and the 3rd weekend of September.
quote: from 10 to 18h Tuesday to Sunday ... In July and August, it is open every day from 10h to 18h ... Combined museum and temporary exhibition admission is €5

claim: Dinant's Maison de la Pataphonie offers public sessions on Sundays, holidays and school holidays at 14:00 and 16:00, plus reserved slots on Wednesdays and the first Sunday of each month, in an instrumentarium by luthier Max Vandervorst built from everyday objects.
quote: Sundays, public holidays and school holidays at 2:00 PM and 4:00 PM ... unique instrumentarium, imagined by wild luthier Max Vandervorst

claim: Maredret Abbey's church is open daily for individual visits; French-language guided tours (1h-1h30) run the first Sunday of each month April-October, and the monastic shop sells abbey beer, jams, honey, ceramics and the famous Maredret illuminations.
quote: L'église est ouverte tous les jours pour une visite individuelle ... Les visites guidées se font tous les premiers dimanches du mois à partir d'avril jusqu'à octobre

claim: Profondeville to Maredsous is roughly 10 km as the crow flies and about 17 km by road, putting Maredsous/Maredret well within the 30 km radius of Arbre.
quote: Approximately 10.4 km in a straight line (as the crow flies) ... 17.21 km by car

claim: Lesse kayak descents (Dinant Evasion) run daily 4 April to 31 October 2026, with three routes: 9 km Houyet-Gendron, 12 km Gendron-Anseremme, 21 km Houyet-Anseremme; the 12 km is closed only on the first Saturday of June (6 June 2026).
quote: The descents of the Lesse (12 km) are available every day from 4 April 2026 to 31 October 2026, except on the first Saturday in June (6 June 2026). The 9 km trip ends September 28, and the 21 km trip concludes October 5.

claim: Lesse kayak descent 2026 pricing is €27–31/person for the 12 km Gendron-Anseremme route and up to €41 for the 21 km Houyet-Anseremme, with 1000–3500 kayaks per day in summer.
quote: The Lesse kayak descent costs €27-31 per person for 12km (Gendron-Celles to Anseremme route), or up to €41 for the longer 21km option... 1000-3500 kayaks per day in summer.

claim: Kayak Libert at Quai de Meuse 1, 5500 Anseremme now operates in partnership with Dinant Evasion; the ticket office moved to rue du vélodrome 15 with free parking.
quote: Billing moved to Dinant Evasion partner location at rue du vélodrome 15, with complimentary parking. Address: Quai de Meuse 1, 5500 Anseremme (Dinant), Belgium. Phone: +32(0)82 22 61 86.

claim: Dinant–Anseremme Meuse cruise is 45 minutes, €13 adult / €12.50 senior / €10 child, with hourly departures 11:30–16:30 daily 25 April–30 August and weekends/holidays in shoulder season.
quote: For the Dinant-Anseremme cruise, adults pay €13, seniors (60+) pay €12.50, and children pay €10... runs for 45 minutes. From April 25 to August 30, it operates every day with departures every hour between 11:30 and 16:30.

claim: Dinant Evasion also offers a 2-hour Dinant–Freÿr cruise (€22 adult, €20 senior, €17 child) and a 3h30 combined cruise + Freÿr Castle visit; license-free electric boat rental is available as well.
quote: Dinant-Freÿr Cruise - Duration: 2 hours... Dinant-Freÿr Cruise + Castle Visit - Duration: 3 hours 30 minutes... take the helm of one of the free license electric boats, or settle down comfortably for a commented cruise.

claim: RAVeL Dinant–Namur (EuroVelo 19 / La Meuse à vélo) is roughly 28–30 km, flat, mostly off-road along the Meuse, passing Profondeville's imposing rocks, Dave Castle and six locks.
quote: Along this Citadels route, mainly on the path of the Meuse RAVeL away from motor traffic... beautiful villas by the riverside and imposing rocks at Profondville, plus the 19th century Dave Castle and six locks along the way.

claim: Pro Velo Namur (Place de la Station 1, 5000 Namur) rents classic, electric, folding and cargo bikes, open Mon–Fri 09:00–12:30 and 13:30–18:00; reachable at 081 81 38 48 / namur@provelo.org.
quote: Pro Velo Namur is located at Place de la Station, 1 – 5000 Namur, and is open Monday to Friday from 09:00 – 12:30 and 13:30 – 18:00... offers all types of bike for rental – classic, electric, folding and cargo bikes.

claim: Citadelle de Namur cable car charges €5.50 one-way / €8.00 return for adults, €4.00/€6.50 seniors, €4.00/€6.00 minors, with reduced-mobility €3.50/€5.00 and infants free.
quote: Adults (18–64): €5.50 / €8.00; Seniors (65+): €4.00 / €6.50; Children (4–5 years): €3.50 / €5.00; Minors/Students (6–17, 18+ with card): €4.00 / €6.00; Persons with reduced mobility: €3.50 / €5.00.

claim: The Namur cable car runs daily 9:30–18:00 in high season (1 April–30 September) and from 9:30 in low season; weekdays it operates 07:00–18:30 for commuters.
quote: The cable car operates from 9:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. during high season (April 1 to September 30) every day... Every weekday, the Téléphérique is open from 7:00 am until 6:30 pm.

claim: The Via Ferrata of Marche-les-Dames (Rochers du Camp Commando) is only accessible weekends and public holidays, requires a Belgian climbing federation card plus valid ID, and visitor capacity is capped daily.
quote: Le week-end et les jours fériés... Visitors must possess both an affiliation card from a Belgian climbing federation and a valid ID. Daily visitor capacity is limited.

claim: The Marche-les-Dames via ferrata, the country's second most important rock site, runs 2.3 km along the Meuse and features vertical sections, footbridges, monkey/Nepali bridges and abseiling, suitable from age 10 with a guide.
quote: Marche-Les-Dames is the second most important rock site in the country, extending over 2 km 300 along the left bank of the Meuse... vertical portions, pendulum, footbridges, monkey bridges, vertiginous crossing, abseiling and Nepali bridges... people as young as 10.

claim: Rochers de Freÿr, just south of Anseremme, is Belgium's most important climbing crag with 7 main and 8 secondary buttresses, 600+ routes from grade 3 to 8c+ on 110 m high limestone overlooking the Meuse.
quote: The 110m high 'kalk' limestone site counts of 7 main crags and 8 secondary crags, with over 600 routes in all varieties... from 3 to 8c+.

claim: Freÿr has been a destination climbing area since the 1920s with over 1000 pitches on compact grey-and-white limestone, equipped by the Belgian Rebolting Team but retaining 3–4 m run-outs on classic routes.
quote: Known as a destination climbing area since the 1920's, there's over 600 routes, 1000 pitches, on various buttresses, towers and faces on beautiful limestone overlooking the Meuse River.

claim: Around Profondeville, the most popular hike is Les Sept Meuses Loop (7.3 km, ~2 hours) with panoramic views of the Meuse bends; La Sibérie loop (10.5 km, moderate) is a local favorite, and trails take in the Rochers de Frêne belvedere.
quote: the most popular hiking route is Les Sept Meuses Loop, a 4.5 mile (7.3 km) trail that takes 2 hours 4 minutes to complete... La Sibérie — loop from Profondeville, a moderate 6.5 mile (10.5 km) path... Rochers de Frêne Belvedere.

claim: Adventure Valley Durbuy lies ~44 km (air line) from Namur and roughly 50+ km by road from Profondeville, placing it outside the 30 km radius of L'Eau Vive.
quote: The shortest distance (air line) between Durbuy and Namur is 27.35 mi (44.02 km).

claim: 2026 cave-only adult ticket €29, child (4-11) €22; combined PassHan (cave + wildlife park) €41.50 adult / €31.50 child; PassHan+ adding Tree Experience €50/€40; under 4 free.
quote: Cave Adult: €29.00 Child (4-11 years): €22.00 ... PassHan (Cave + Wildlife Park) Adult: €41.50 Child (4-11 years): €31.50 ... PassHan+ Adult: €50.00 Child (4-11 years): €40.00

claim: Domaine des Grottes de Han open 10:00–15:00 with shorter waits before 11am/after 2pm; seasonal closure from 12 November 2026; 20% e-ticket discount if booked before 28/02.
quote: open from 10:00 - 15:00 with reduced waiting times before 11am and after 2pm. There is a seasonal closure from November 12, 2026 ... -20% discount on all e-tickets if you buy before 28/02

claim: Chevetogne 2026 entry: NATURE day €14/car or €11/person online; LEISURE day €12/person on-site or €11 online; FUN day (summer pools open) €17/person on-site or €16 online; children 0-5 free.
quote: NATURE Days ... 14€/véhicule or €11/person online ... LEISURE Days ... 12€/pers. or €11/person online ... FUN Days (July 4–Aug 23, 2026) ... 17€/pers. or €16/person online ... Children 0-5: Free

claim: Domaine Provincial de Chevetogne spans ~600 ha and packs 14 themed playgrounds, two museums, gardens, walking trails and outdoor recreation for families.
quote: Domaine provincial de Chevetogne

claim: Réserve naturelle de Furfooz open daily 10:00–16:30 from 4 April to 1 November 2026; adults €7.50, students €5, children 6-12 €2, under-6 free; 3.5 km marked trail taking 1–2 hours.
quote: From 4 April to 1 November 2026 Open daily from 10:00 am to 4:30 pm ... Adults: €7.50 ... Children (6-12): €2 ... 3.5 km marked pathway requiring between one and two hours

claim: Furfooz reserve combines caves (Trou du Grand Duc, Trou des Nutons, Trou du Frontal), Roman baths, megalithic remains and a fortified spur on a single ticket; pushchairs not permitted and not wheelchair-accessible.
quote: Le tarif par personne est de 5€, et 1€ pour les moins de 12 ans ... Trou du Grand Duc, le Trou des Nutons et le Trou du Frontal sont aujourd'hui visitables

claim: Grotte la Merveilleuse in Dinant: adult €10, child €6, ~50-minute self-guided circuit through 650m of accessible galleries; open daily 11:00–17:00 in summer.
quote: Adults: 10€, Children: 6€ ... The visit lasts approximately 50 minutes ... self-guided tour ... 650 meters of galleries out of a total of 850 are accessible

claim: Grottes de Goyet 2026: open Sundays/holidays and daily during Belgian school holidays 15 Feb–8 Nov; departures at 11h and 14h; adults €13, children 3-12 €10, seniors €11; ~90-min visit with ~200 steps, reservation mandatory.
quote: Ouvert tous les dimanches et jours fériés du 15 février jusqu'au 8 novembre 2026 ... Adults (18-64): €13 Children (3-12): €10 ... Approximately 90 minutes ... roughly 200 steps

claim: Goyet is among the few European sites yielding both Neanderthal and Homo sapiens fossils and now features a multimedia walk through seven galleries with light projections and soundscapes.
quote: expérience multimédia et sensorielle avec nouvelles lumières, projections sur les parois et ambiances auditives, à travers sept galeries

claim: Espace de l'Homme de Spy (interpretation centre on the Spy Neandertal discovery site) at Onoz opens Wed-Sun 13:00–17:00; €5 adult, €3 ages 6-18, free under 6.
quote: du mercredi au dimanche, de 13h à 17h ... Adultes : 5 € ... 6-18 ans et étudiants : 3 €. Gratuité pour les enfants de moins de 6 ans

claim: Spy Cave (Jemeppe-sur-Sambre, Namur) is a classified Walloon Heritage site where 1886 Neanderthal fossil finds drove a 19th-century scientific paradigm shift.
quote: Classified as a premier Heritage site of the Walloon Region, the location ranks among the most significant paleolithic sites in Europe ... In 1886 Neanderthal fossils of excellent quality were discovered

claim: The Citadelle de Dinant cable car — long Belgium's only one — has been closed since 26 October on safety grounds and needs a complete renovation; future replacement (funicular or elevator) under study.
quote: Funiculaire, ascenseur… quel futur pour le téléphérique de la Citadelle de Dinant ?

claim: Grottes de Floreffe described as among the largest semi-dolomitic caves in Belgium; visits Saturday/Sunday year-round by appointment, duration ~1 hour.
quote: les visites sont disponibles toute l'année, le samedi et dimanche sur rendez-vous. La visite dure une heure

claim: Driving distance Dinant ↔ Profondeville (Arbre is a Profondeville section) is 17 km, placing Dinant, Furfooz and the Lesse valley sites well within a 30-km radius while Han-sur-Lesse sits at ~35 km.
quote: The distance from Dinant to Profondeville is 17 kilometres by road

claim: Mont-Fat in Dinant historically hosted a chairlift-served attraction park and tower with Meuse-valley views, but the site is currently caught up in a contested holiday-village redevelopment and operations are uncertain.
quote: Mont-Fat

claim: The Plus Beaux Villages de Wallonie network officially recognises 33 labelled villages across Wallonia, including Celles, Crupet, Falaën, Mozet, Sosoye, Soulme and Thon-Samson in Namur province.
quote: the association Les Plus Beaux Villages de Wallonie oversees a network of 33 villages, all of which bear a strong territorial identity and reflect traditional architecture

claim: Sosoye sits along meanders of the Molignée with limestone Condroz houses, an 18th-century Nativity church, listed presbytery and 17th-century tithe barn, near Maredsous Abbey.
quote: meanders of the picturesque Molignée with limestone houses typical of the Condroz valley along its main street, surrounded by the steep inclines of the Ranzinelle Mountain

claim: Thon-Samson overlooks the Meuse and Samson valleys and features the 18th-century Forge Castle, ruins of the Samson Fortress on a rocky promontory, and the Scladina prehistoric grotto.
quote: Forge Castle (18th c.), an impressive classical residence with a tower of medieval inspiration, and the ruins of the Samson Fortress standing on a rocky promontory above the confluence of the Samson and Meuse rivers

claim: Mozet is a Namur-province Plus Beaux Villages member with traditional stone architecture set in the Samson valley.
quote: Mozet, yesterday's land, today's stones

claim: Crupet's Grotte Saint-Antoine de Padoue, an artificial grotto built 1900–1903 by villagers under Canon Jules Gérard, stages life-of-the-saint scenes; its devil tableau is the most famous, with free parking and views of the keep behind the Pachis café.
quote: The artificial caves were built between 1900 and 1903 by the inhabitants of the village at the instigation of Canon Jules Gérard... The devil scene, which is very impressive, is the most famous.

claim: Crupet's 13th-century Carondelet keep, converted into a castle-farm in the 16th century and listed since 1973, was restored through 2020; the village has a 2 km interpretation trail and thirteen marked walks of 4–13 km.
quote: The Carondelet keep is a must-see... a 13th-century fortified tower that was converted into a castle-farm in the 16th century... underwent significant renovation work until 2020

claim: Celles, in the Houyet commune of Namur Condroz, is anchored by the 11th-century Collégiale Saint-Hadelin, considered the most perfect expression of Mosan Romanesque art and classified Exceptional Heritage of Wallonia.
quote: Celles, village chef d'œuvre d'art Roman

claim: Falaën in the Molignée valley pairs with the romantic ruins of Montaigle castle (destroyed 1554 by Henry II's troops), with the famous Molignée draisine railbike running from the foot of the castle to the old Maredsous station.
quote: Standing on an abrupt, rocky spur overlooking the pretty Molignée valley, the Montaigle site is one of the loveliest examples of the medieval castle so dear to the Romantics

claim: Soulme, perched above the Hermeton valley with Fagne-style architecture, features the listed 11th-century St. Columba church, a 17th/18th-century mill and the former monks' farm, and is a launchpad for rural walks.
quote: Perched at the summit of its hilltop overlooking the Hermeton valley, Soulme features typical Fagne architecture nestled in a verdant setting

claim: The Maison du Patrimoine Médiéval Mosan in Bouvignes-sur-Meuse (Place du Bailliage 16, 5500 Dinant) opens Tue–Sun 10:00–18:00 (April–October) or 10:00–17:00 (November–March); adults €8, audioguides in FR/NL/EN, typical visit 1.5 h.
quote: From April 1 to October 31: Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM. From November 1 to March 31: Tuesday to Sunday, 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM

claim: Dinant's Charles de Gaulle bridge is decorated since 2010 with 28 oversized painted saxophones, each placed before a national flag honouring a member country, paying tribute to Adolphe Sax (born Dinant 1814, saxophone patented 1846).
quote: Installed in 2010, 28 saxophones adorn the Charles de Gaulle bridge. Painted in unique colors, one saxophone takes on the appearance of a basketball, another looks like a mermaid

claim: Namur's Halle al'Chair, a late-16th-century Mosan-Renaissance red-brick-and-stone hall built 1588–1590 by Bastien Sion and Conrad de Nuremberg as a butchers' market, today houses the Namur Tourist Office at the foot of the Citadel.
quote: The Halle al'Chair is an architectural marvel by the Sambre River, originally a butcher's hub from 1588 to 1590, and it now houses the Namur Tourist Office

claim: Namur's old-town rue de Fer is the city's main shopping street running off Place de l'Ange, and the nearby Baroque Saint-Loup church (17th c.) is considered one of Belgium's most beautiful Baroque interiors.
quote: Rue de Fer is also where you'll find public toilets and the City Hall... The Saint-Loup Catholic Church, a 17th-century church and one of the most beautiful Baroque buildings in Belgium

claim: Wépion is Belgium's strawberry capital; the Musée de la Fraise hosts exhibits on history and cultivation plus a berry garden with 15 strawberry varieties, with English translations and a gift shop of strawberry liqueurs and jams.
quote: the village of Wépion, and teaches visitors all about the tasty fruit... The museum also boasts a berry garden with 15 varieties of strawberries

claim: The Rochers de Frênes belvedere on the Lustin/Profondeville bank towers roughly 100 m above the Meuse, with limestone cliffs once 800 m high before river erosion, offering the iconic Meuse panorama opposite Profondeville church.
quote: The rocks are an impressive peak about 100 meters above the Meuse, with limestone formations that culminated at 800 meters millions of years ago before being eroded by the Meuse river

claim: The Promenade des 7 Meuses is a 7.3–7.5 km loop between Lustin and Godinne stations (~2 h 30, 170 m climb) combining forest and Ravel sections that reaches a viewpoint over seven Meuse meanders, also used by paragliders.
quote: At the famous Les Sept Meuses viewpoint, you can see seven meanders of the Meuse, and on clear days the view extends to the French border

claim: Profondeville's seasonal Belle de Frênes passage d'eau rows visitors across the Meuse opposite the Rochers de Frênes massif, giving water-level views of the cliffs.
quote: Le passage d'eau à Profondeville

claim: Saint-Joseph visitor centre at Maredsous Abbey (Rue de Maredsous 11, 5537 Denée) offers a 90-min tasting tour of microbrewery, hops farm and cheese-making museum ending with 4 galopins paired with cheese; tours run weekends, public holidays and school holidays.
quote: The tasting tour (90 minutes) includes the microbrewery, hops farm, cheese-making museum, and a tasting of "4 galopins or soft drinks" paired with cheese. Tours operate "on weekends, public holidays and during school holidays."

claim: Brasserie Caracole in Falmignoul is open Saturday and Sunday 2:00 PM–5:30 PM (weekdays 8:30–12:00 and 13:00–17:30, with a Friday evening 18:30–21:30 slot).
quote: Weekdays (Monday-Friday): 8:30 AM – 12:00 PM and 1:00 PM – 5:30 PM ... Friday Extended: An additional evening slot from 6:30 PM – 9:30 PM ... Weekends (Saturday-Sunday): 2:00 PM – 5:30 PM

claim: Brasserie Caracole (Côte Marie-Thérèse 86, 5500 Falmignoul) is an artisanal brewery using 18th-century methods with copper tanks heated on wood fire, producing La Caracole, La Troublette, La Saxo and La Nostradamus; guided tours with tastings available in EN/FR/NL/DE.
quote: Côte Marie-Thérèse 86, 5500 Falmignoul ... "copper tanks heated on wood fire." ... The brewery produces "La Caracole," "La Troublette," "La Saxo," and "La Nostradamus."

claim: Brasserie du Bocq (Rue de la Brasserie 4, 5530 Purnode), founded 1858, brews Blanche de Namur and the Gauloise range but no longer offers tourist visits to the brewery facility.
quote: Blanche de Namur (4.5% ABV) - Award-winning wheat beer; Gauloise series (Blonde, Brune, Ambrée) ... "As our new facilities no longer allow us to receive visitors, we no longer organise tourist visits to the Brewery."

claim: A third-party listing notes Bocq is no longer authorised to host tourist visits, so plan to taste Gauloise/Blanche de Namur off-site (in Namur bars or at retailers) rather than at Purnode.
quote: The brewery is "no longer allowed to receive visitors and organize tourist visit," according to a comment on their WhichMuseum page.

claim: Musée de la Fraise (Chaussée de Dinant 1037, Namur/Wépion) opens April–September Tue–Sun 11 AM–6 PM (Oct–Mar Tue–Fri 1–5 PM); admission €5, free first Sunday of each month; includes Jardin des petits fruits.
quote: April to September: Tuesday-Sunday, 11 am–6 pm ... October to March: Tuesday-Friday, 1–5 pm ... "The museum remains accessible and free each first Sunday of the month" ... Admission: €5

claim: Wépion strawberry season runs May (under tunnels/greenhouses) through October, peaking in June, governed by the Groupement des Fraisiéristes Wallons.
quote: the first strawberries of May are harvested thanks to greenhouses or plastic tunnels, June is meant for unforced and field production, and from July to October, harvests from the seedlings extend the growing season

claim: Couque de Dinant is an extremely hard biscuit of equal-weight wheat flour and honey, moulded with pear/walnut/beech wooden moulds into animal, floral and landscape motifs; broken into fragments or soaked in coffee rather than bitten.
quote: The traditional recipe contains only two components in equal weight: wheat flour and honey ... These are "extremely hard" biscuits ... consumers "break [them] into fragments" or "soak [them] in coffee." ... Wooden molds from pear, walnut, or beech wood create diverse designs

claim: Maison Jacobs has produced couques de Dinant on Rue Grande in Dinant since 1860 — one of the three remaining houses, twice rebuilt after WWI and WWII bomb damage.
quote: Established since 1860 on Rue Grande, Maison Jacobs is one of the three remaining houses still producing these famous biscuits.

claim: Couques V. Collard, the oldest producer (since 1774), is located at Rue En-Rhée 24, Dinant — a second couque address to visit alongside Jacobs.
quote: The business is located at Rue En-Rhée 24, Dinant, Namur, Belgium. The Collard Family prepares and sells them from generation to generation since 1774.

claim: Flamiche dinantaise is a savoury cheese tart made with Boulette de Romedenne, butter and 13–15 eggs; the Confrérie des Quarteniers de la Flamiche Dinantaise (founded 1956) runs an annual September eating contest.
quote: 500 grams of Boulette de Romedenne (a pungent local cheese), 250 grams of butter and lots of eggs, 13 eggs for a smaller version (30 cm) and 15 eggs for a larger version (35 cm) ... the Confrérie des Quarteniers de la Flamiche Dinantaise - the Brotherhood of the Flamiche (founded in 1956) - organizes an annual flamiche eating competition

claim: Namur's Saturday market (now branded "Marché du Bord de l'Eau") has moved permanently to Boulevard Frère Orban along the Sambre between Pont de l'Évêché and Pont de la Libération, drawing ~5,000 clients weekly — no longer on Place de l'Ange.
quote: New Location: Boulevard Frère Orban, along the Sambre River (between Pont de l'Évêché and Pont de la Libération) ... New Name: "Marché du Bord de l'Eau" ... Approximately 5,000 clients visit the market weekly.

claim: Namur's main weekly market runs Saturdays 8:30 AM–1:00 PM, with smaller weekday markets across the commune.
quote: The main market of Namur takes place on Saturdays from 8:30 AM to 1:00 PM at boulevard Frère Orban along the Sambre.

claim: The historic Fromagerie du Samson at Goyet (Gesves) moved in 2021 to Marche-en-Famenne as L'Atelier de la Fromagerie du Samson, producing ~40 raw-milk Walloon cheeses under Vincent Verleyen — so day-trippers should source Samson cheeses via Namur fromageries or the Maredsous shop rather than at Goyet.
quote: L'Atelier de la Fromagerie du Samson, based in Marche-en-Famenne, Wallonia, artisanally creates and ages about forty varieties of cheeses exclusively from raw milk collected from local producers

claim: Distillerie de Namur-Bossimé is a micro-distillery at Rue Bossimé 2B, 5101 Loyers (Namur), making fruit eaux-de-vie, liqueurs and 'The Blackbird's Gin' with Wépion strawberry, with no artificial flavour or colour.
quote: Rue Bossimé, 2B, 5101, Loyers ... The Blackbird's gin à la fraise de wépion ... sans colorants, sans arômes artificiels, sans exhausteurs de goûts

claim: Wave Distil is a craft distillery at Grand'route de Ciney 104, 5503 Dinant, producing the Ginneke'Tiche London dry gin and Manneke'Tiche pure malt whisky.
quote: Grand'route de Ciney, 104 5503 Dinant BELGIQUE

claim: Wave Distil welcomes visitors by appointment in groups, runs masterclass tastings and opened a Gourmet Bistro inside the distillery in October 2023.
quote: It is possible to visit the distillery, but only by group, by appointment, and it offers events such as Masterclass tastings, private or professional evenings, teambuilding and gourmet bistro meals.

claim: Wave Distil in Sorinnes/Dinant launched its Ginneke'Tiche gin in 2022, distilled from local Belgian barley.
quote: Dinant : du gin distillé à partir d'un orge local

claim: VisitWallonia lists craft distilleries open for tours including Belgian Owl (Fexhe, single malt whisky) and Distillerie de Biercée (Ragnies, eaux-de-vie and liqueurs) — both more than 30 km from Profondeville.
quote: The Owl Distillery ... Single Malt Whisky 100 % belge distillé dans des alambics écossais ... Distillerie de Biercée - Ragnies ... eaux-de-vie et liqueurs

claim: Dinant Evasion enforces strict Lesse-kayak rules: no cool boxes/barbecues/beer crates, no stopping outside marked zones, no fires, no littering, with kayaks ID-tagged to renters — yet more than 10 rubbish bags are still collected weekly from the banks.
quote: strictly forbidden: To take cool boxes, portable barbecues or beer crates on board ... more than 10 rubbish bags are collected every week on the banks of the Lesse

claim: The Lesse kayak descent has been suspended in recent dry summers; since July 2023 the 21 km and 9 km Houyet runs were halted by drought to protect flora and fauna.
quote: La descente de la Lesse en canoë-kayak suspendue en raison de la sécheresse

claim: Minimum flow thresholds for navigation are only 2 m³/s Houyet–Gendron and 1.5 m³/s Gendron–Anseremme — so low that kayaks scrape the bottom, prompting Wallonia to commission a study to raise the thresholds.
quote: Kayaks qui touchent le fond: faut-il rehausser les débits seuils de la Lesse par temps de sécheresse?

claim: During the 2023 drought only the 12 km Gendron–Anseremme run remained open; the longer Houyet routes were closed.
quote: Sécheresse de la Lesse: un seul parcours kayak reste praticable, le 12 km au départ de Gendron

claim: Visitor reviews of Dinant Evasion's Lesse descents describe overcrowding ('you could barely see the river … so many kayaks') and chaotic docking at portages.
quote: you could barely see the river at certain times because so many kayaks sailed on it ... chaos when docking
